paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by language models before and after instruction tuning, categorized by three types of contact: Support of Authorities, Extended Contact, and Virtual Contact. Each category contains four bars representing different conditions: "No Contact Before" (light gray), "Positive Contact Before" (light red), "Negative Contact Before" (light blue), and their corresponding "After" conditions (darker shades: dark gray, dark red, dark blue). The y-axis represents "Bias Percentage," ranging from 0 to 70, with values labeled on top of each bar. For "Support of Authorities," the bias percentages before tuning are 39.50%, 31.83%, and 42.38% for the three contact types, while after tuning, they drop to 0.04%, 0.00%, and 0.00%, respectively. Similarly, for "Extended Contact," the bias percentages decrease from 40.61%, 36.13%, and 47.28% to 0.00%, 0.00%, and 0.11%. In the "Virtual Contact" category, bias percentages before tuning are 39.74%, 39.17%, and 43.83%, and after tuning, they are 10.00%, 10.01%, and 10.02%. The chart shows that instruction tuning significantly reduces bias across all categories, especially for Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, where bias is reduced to nearly zero, while a notable residual bias remains in Virtual Contact. The darker shaded bars (after tuning) are positioned on top of the lighter shaded bars (before tuning), visually indicating the reduction in bias.
